title: Solving account executive challenges on Mac: how to fix your daily workflow
metaTitle: Account Executive Challenges: How to Solve Problems on Mac Efficiently
description: Learn how to overcome common account executive challenges on your Mac. Discover real fixes for context switching and administrative burnout to improve your performance.
intro: Account executive challenges often stem from the constant cognitive strain of context switching and document chasing throughout your workday. You likely spend hours toggling between Gmail, Slack, and your CRM, which prevents you from focusing on the high-value problem solving required to close deals.
tldr: Account executives spend up to 75% of their day in meetings, leaving little time for deep work.
Context switching between disconnected apps costs you 3 to 5 hours of productivity every single week.
Burnout from administrative tasks can cost employers over $20,000 per executive annually.
Structured time blocking and using a single source of truth for client data are the best free ways to improve.
Lazur helps by keeping your focus on the screen and providing quick answers without you needing to switch apps.

blocks.text: The core of your struggle is structural. You are asked to be a relationship manager, a data entry clerk, and a strategic planner all at once. When you move from a Zoom call to a Slack message and then to a Google Sheet, your brain loses momentum. This is known as context switching. It is not a personal failure. It is the result of using a stack of tools that do not talk to each other.
The cost of reactive problem solving

When you react to every notification, you lose the ability to solve complex problems. You end up applying quick fixes to deep issues. This cycle keeps you in a state of high stress. Research shows that 82% of knowledge workers are at risk of burnout because they never get the recovery time they need to think clearly.
If you work in a regulated industry, always check your company data policy before using AI tools. Ensure you are not sharing sensitive client information with third-party servers.

items: Use the How might we framework to define your problems clearly before starting to type.
Block out 90 minutes of your morning for deep work in your calendar. Do not check Slack or email during this time.
Create a single document in Notion or a dedicated folder for each account. Keep all links and notes there to stop searching through your drive.
Close all browser tabs that are not related to your current task. Use Safari tab groups to keep your sales research separate from your internal admin tasks.

faq.question: How do I stop context switching?
faq.answer: Start by grouping your tasks. Do all your email replies in one 30-minute block rather than checking your inbox every time a notification appears.

faq.question: Is Lazur safe for my sales data?

costs.title: Lost productivity
costs.text: You lose 3 to 5 hours every week just by clicking between different apps and trying to remember where you left off.

costs.title: Burnout risk
costs.text: The mental fatigue of constant task switching puts you at higher risk for burnout and disengagement from your work.

causes.title: Tool fragmentation
causes.text: Your CRM, email, and communication apps do not share data, forcing you to manually copy and paste information.

causes.title: Reactive culture
causes.text: The expectation to answer every Slack message instantly prevents you from doing the deep work needed for complex problem solving.

fixes.title: Time blocking
fixes.text: Set aside two 90-minute blocks daily for deep work. Turn off notifications in Slack using the Focus mode in macOS.

fixes.title: Contextual documentation
fixes.text: Use a single document for each account to track decisions. This stops you from searching through old email threads.
